title: Monodromy and ambient exactness of torsion local systems
statement: Let $S$ be a nonempty connected Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], let $\bar s$ be a geometric point, and let $G=\pi_1(S,\bar s)$ with its profinite topology [def-galois-fibre-functor]. Let $R$ be a commutative ring annihilated by an integer $n>0$. Work with $R_S$-module sheaves on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Call such a sheaf a local system if its underlying sheaf of sets is a filtered colimit of sheaves represented by finite etale $S$-schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. A discrete continuous $R$-linear $G$-module is an $R$-module with a $G$-action by $R$-linear automorphisms such that every element has open stabilizer; morphisms are equivariant linear maps. The geometric stalk functor gives an additive equivalence from these local systems to these modules. It preserves and reflects short exact sequences, computed in ambient module sheaves and in underlying $R$-modules, respectively, and commutes with all small colimits. Ambient kernels and cokernels of maps of local systems are local systems. An extension in ambient $R_S$-module sheaves of two local systems is a local system. The corresponding assertions on disconnected Noetherian schemes hold component by component. A constant sheaf is a local system and corresponds to trivial monodromy. For a connected finite etale cover $c:T\to S$, pullback of local systems corresponds to restricting the action to the open subgroup $c_*\pi_1(T,\bar t)$; in particular $c^{-1}L$ is constant if and only if this subgroup acts trivially on $L_{\bar s}$. Conversely, if $L$ is any $R_S$-module sheaf, not assumed to be a local system, such that $c^{-1}L$ is a local system on $T$ (for instance a constant sheaf on $T$), then $L$ is a local system on $S$. Finally, among local systems, a sheaf is locally constant of finite type [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules] if and only if its stalk at $\bar s$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. In that case it becomes constant on a connected finite etale Galois cover [def-galois-object]. No finiteness of the set $R$ or of general local-system stalks is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Definitions 7.2.1 and Propositions 7.2.2-7.2.5, pp. 301-303 (descent along a surjective finite etale cover: 7.2.4, p. 302); finite-generation assertion: a discrete continuous action on a finitely generated module has a common open normal stabilizer of a finite generating set. This is the ind-finite local-system category, not every etale-locally constant sheaf.
